mechanism: per-part retirement clock→dimensions/visibility→multipart display cleanup; not armor physical detachment
producer: Naga constructs12 NagaSegment children and assigns multipart IDs after spawn packet. Segments are explicitly ticked by parent moveSegments rather than ordinary world tick entities.

setSegmentsPerHealth compares health-derived count; reduced tail elements receive (oldCount-index)*12 selfDestruct counters, so higher indices expire first; increases reactivate segments. This countdown is not a new species or independent animation reference per segment.

moveSegments ticks every part and follows previous leader at distance2; dead/dying zeroes straightenForce, but following positions still compute. Do not claim complete frozen pose or gravity-driven separation.
part_consumer: NagaSegment.tick decrements local deathCounter; atzero calls parent.makePoofAt(part.position), sound, parent.deathTime=0 then deactivate. deactivate sets dimensions0x0 and invisibletrue; activation restores2x2. Armor pile behavior is absent.
Active segment hurt forwards2/3 to parent and collision attacks living targets; these are gameplay multiparts. Cosmetic armor must not adopt those hitboxes, attack, drops, or extra server entities.

Part remove is parent-owned: Naga.remove kills children on server. TFPart writes position/rotation/dimensions/dirty synced data; readData interpolates position/rotation over3 steps and refreshes dimensions. Exact packet producer/receiver missing locally; late tracking synchronization cannot be certified.
body_render_chain: TFPartRenderer.extractRenderState copies perpart rotation/death/overlay/invisibility-related fields; submit applies transformations and calls model.setupAnim(state), then renderType may suppress invisible output. NagaSegmentRenderer additionally skips submit entirely when state.isInvisible, interpolates shortest yaw, pitches, scales2 and translates.
NagaModel has one16cube at64x32 atlas; child segment geometry is not a bone detached from head, it is a separate multipart model display. No texture content viewed.
Head renderer scale2.01; flipDegrees0 prevents normal keel-over; texture selects dazed, charging or death state. This is not a head/neck death keyframe sequence.
death_reload_boundaries: BaseTFBoss selected tickDeath increments deathTime on both sides, server checks completion/remove and client runs visual tick; Naga completion threshold24+100=124. Segment expiration resets parent deathTime, so nominal124 is not sufficient to assert actual total death duration.

Naga segment countdown is not separately stored in the read empty add/readAdditionalSaveData; Naga has no own save override. Parent base selected save stores home/deathitems and delegates inherited behavior. Parent startSeen sends UpdateDeathTimePacket, but source absent; do not infer complete countdown persistence, reload or late tracking correctness.
Naga client death particles trace a path toward boss chest, ground clip from+2 to-3 includes water then emitsCOMPOSTER. This is not an armor pile or rising ghostflame.
application: Reuse concept of separate perpiece visibility/completion, clear removed pieces atparent removal, and do not confuse independent clock with world-space detach.
